scenes.heading: Repeated digits, palindromes and repunits
scenes.narration: A palindrome reads the same from either end. Matching digits sit in paired places on either side of its centre. A repunit is made entirely of ones. Place value lets us build a repeated digit with one multiplication.

beats.cue: A palindrome reads the same from either end. Matching digits sit in paired places on either side of its centre.
beats.line: Mirror the digits about the centre.

beats.cue: A repunit is made entirely of ones. Place value lets us build a repeated digit with one multiplication.
beats.line: A repunit has a one in every place.

scenes.heading: Where this idea helps
scenes.narration: In AMC Upper Primary practice, watch for numbers that read the same when reversed, or a long row of repeated digits. In a Rossmoyne style puzzle, add a divisibility rule. Use the mirror structure to leave fewer free choices.

scenes.heading: Build a repeated digit
scenes.narration: Take the repunit one hundred and eleven and multiply by three. What number will you get? Picture multiplying each place separately. Look for any place that would need a carry.

beats.cue: Take the repunit one hundred and eleven and multiply by three. What number will you get?
Picture multiplying each place separately. Look for any place that would need a carry.
beats.line: Can any column make a carry?

scenes.heading: Build a repeated digit
scenes.narration: Each one becomes a three. The product in every column is below ten, so no digit has to move into the next place. The answer is three hundred and thirty-three. You can view it as one copy of that digit in every position.

scenes.heading: Spot a factor in a palindrome
scenes.narration: The four-digit number two thousand seven hundred and seventy-two reads the same both ways. Divide it by eleven. Can you find the quotient by splitting the outer and inner pairs of digits?

beats.cue: The four-digit number two thousand seven hundred and seventy-two reads the same both ways. Divide it by eleven.
Can you find the quotient by splitting the outer and inner pairs of digits?
beats.line: Separate the outside and inside digits.

scenes.heading: Spot a factor in a palindrome
scenes.narration: The two outer copies of two contribute two thousand and two. The two inner copies of seven contribute seven hundred and seventy. One thousand and one is eleven times ninety-one. One hundred and ten is eleven times ten. Both pairs share a factor of eleven. Now add ninety-one times two and ten times seven. The quotient is two hundred and fifty-two.

scenes.heading: Count palindromes that pass a test
scenes.narration: Count the five-digit palindromes divisible by nine whose first digit is at most nine. The first and last digits match. So do the second and fourth. The centre can be any single digit allowed by the divisibility test.

beats.line: Five places: A, B, C, B, A

scenes.heading: Count palindromes that pass a test
scenes.narration: A five-digit palindrome is fixed once we choose its first two digits and the centre. Call them A, B and C. The digit sum is twice A plus twice B plus C. For each outer pair choose C to make the sum a multiple of nine. There is always a choice from zero through eight, since those digits give all nine remainders. Nine is a second choice precisely when zero already worked. That happens when A plus B is itself divisible by nine.

scenes.heading: Check the challenge solution
scenes.narration: The pair can sum to nine, with one partner from zero to eight for each allowed first digit. The pair nine and nine also sums to eighteen. Add ninety and ten. The answer is one hundred, with each number counted once by its three free positions.

scenes.heading: Common mistakes
scenes.narration: Starting with zero would give fewer than five written digits. Only the centre and the second digit may start from zero in this count. When the required remainder is zero, both zero and nine work as centre digits. Test those two endpoints before you count.

scenes.heading: Your exam checklist
scenes.narration: Write only the independent digits first. Use the mirror pairs to copy the other positions. Use the divisibility test on the resulting digit sum. Check whether the residue allows two single digits.
